newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian AvtoVAZ shareholders to vote on new issue.
newsitem.headline: Russian AvtoVAZ shareholders to vote on new issue.

text.p: Russian automobile manufacturer AvtoVAZ said on Thursday it will ask shareholders to vote on the issue of about 27 million new shares at a meeting on August 2 as part of a plan to restructure its debt to the government.
An AvtoVAZ statement said the shares will be transferred to the government in return for a 10-year extension of the deadline by which AvtoVAZ must pay off its debt.

The statement said the decision to grant the extension was taken at a meeting of a government commission headed by First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais. No confirmation was immediately available.

Faced with a gaping hole in the 1997 budget and battling with parliament over painful cuts in spending, the government has threatened to bankrupt companies which do not pay taxes or restructure their debt.

Under a government plan to restructure company debt, the companies must issue new equity comprising a controlling stake to be held as collateral by the state, or company debt that can also be held by the state.
If the companies fail to pay off their debt, the government can sell the shares or bonds.
AvtoVAZ is one of Russia's biggest debtors, with a debt to the government of 2.81 trillion roubles ($487.2 million) as of June 1, 1997.
